title: Grace softens rigor: precise duty for attainable measure; vow-and-endeavor for degrees beyond ordinary grace
source_text: XL. Tertio foedus gratiae, etsi obligationem istam simpliciter & omnino non tollat, tollere tamen rigorem, seu severitatem & terribilitatem istius obligationis. Quamvis enim, inquit, universam justitiae perfectionem nobis ob oculos ponat ut affectandam, & pro viribus assequendam, non tamen stricte & praecise sub periculo & poena aeternae dam-nationis eam exigit. Nam ad certam quidem obedientiae mensuram, quae videlicet per gratiam ordinariam est possibilis, stricte & praecise, hoc est, sub aeternae damnationis periculo obligat, exigendo ut eam actu habeamus. Ad ulteriorem vero mensuram, quam viribus gratiae ordinariis assequi non possumus, obligat minus stricte, videlicet, exi-gendo ut eam habeamus saltem in voto & conatu. Verbi gratia, ad perfectionem partium, ut vocant, obligat praecise. Nam non aliter vitam aeternam promittit, quam hac conditione ut eam actu habeamus. Ad perfectionem vero eam, quae graduum dicitur, non tam stricte & praecise obligat; sed tantum exigit, ut pro viribus gratiae nobis concessa eam assequi studeamus & conemur.
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly the covenant of grace, although it does not simply and altogether take away that obligation, yet takes away the rigor, or severity and terribleness of that obligation. For although, he says, it sets before our eyes the whole perfection of righteousness as to be aimed at and attained according to our strength, yet it does not exact it strictly and precisely under peril and penalty of eternal damnation. For to a certain measure of obedience which namely is possible through ordinary grace it binds strictly and precisely—that is, under peril of eternal damnation—requiring that we have it in act. But to a further measure which we cannot attain by the ordinary powers of grace it binds less strictly, namely requiring that we have it at least in vow and endeavor. For example, to the perfection of parts, as they call it, it binds precisely. For it does not otherwise promise eternal life than on this condition that we have it in act. But to that perfection which is called of degrees it does not bind so strictly and precisely; but only requires that by the powers of grace granted us we study and endeavor to attain it.
pass_b_english: Grace removes the law’s terror without erasing the duty: attainable ordinary-grace obedience is still exacted under eternal peril.
Beyond that, ‘degrees’ perfection is owed in vow and endeavor—not as a strict act-condition of life.

choices.why: Degrees vs parts: softer obligation, not indifference.
